sources.entry: azure-sdk-for-python - Microsoft Azure SDK for Python, published as per-service packages.

summary.one_liner: Microsoft's monorepo for the Azure SDK for Python, where each Azure service ships as its own separately installable client or management library.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is the active development home for the Azure SDK for Python. Service libraries live under the /sdk directory, and each service has its own set of packages instead of one large Azure package. The README divides packages into Client libraries (for using and interacting with existing resources, such as uploading a blob) and Management libraries (for provisioning and managing Azure resources, identified by namespaces starting with azure-mgmt-). Each category is further split into new releases (GA and preview, built on azure-core and the Azure Identity library) and previous versions (last stable releases with wider service coverage). The README also documents how to opt out of the default telemetry by subclassing UserAgentPolicy and passing it as user_agent_policy when creating a client.
use_cases: Access Azure Blob Storage from Python code
Provision and manage Azure resources programmatically
Authenticate to Azure services from Python apps
Pick a single Azure service library instead of a large bundle
Disable Azure SDK telemetry in a Python client
how_to_run: Browse the service libraries in the /sdk directory
Open the README.md or README.rst in the chosen library's project folder for install and usage instructions
notable: One package per Azure service instead of a single monolithic Azure package
Separates client libraries (data-plane) from management libraries (azure-mgmt-*)
Documented opt-out of default telemetry via a custom UserAgentPolicy subclass
Shared core behaviour (retries, logging, auth, transport) through azure-core
caveats: Repository is for active development; the README recommends public or versioned developer docs for consumers
Telemetry is on by default and must be disabled per client
Some new management libraries changed authentication, requiring migration per the referenced guide
Preview packages are not recommended for production use
